lesson_scope: Relationships between engine power, driving force, and speed (P = Fv and F = P/v); steady-speed motion on level roads and inclined planes where acceleration is zero; instantaneous acceleration calculations using Newton's second law (F - R - mg sin theta = ma); maximum possible speeds under constant and variable power; connected vehicles (towing) with internal towbar tension under steady and accelerated conditions.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Engine power from constant speed on level road

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Engine power from constant speed on level road

hints: At constant speed on a horizontal road, the driving force equals the resistance force: $F = 800\text{ N}$.
Use $P = F v = 800 \times 25 = 20000\text{ W} = 20\text{ kW}$.

walkthrough.text:
State the equilibrium condition at constant velocity along the level road:
$$a = 0 \implies F - R = 0 \implies F = R = 800\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power developed by the engine in kilowatts:
$$P = F v = (800)(25) = 20000\text{ W} = 20\text{ kW}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Match forces at steady speed:
- Zero acceleration means driving force balances resistance:
$$F = 800\text{ N}$$

Compute engine power:
- Multiplying driving force by velocity:
$$P = 800 \times 25 = 20000\text{ W} = 20\text{ kW}$$
The engine operates at $20\text{ kW}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $F = R = 800\text{ N}$ at steady speed and uses $P = F v$.
Obtains engine power $P = 800 \times 25 = 20000\text{ W} = 20\text{ kW}$.

- At $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the driving force is:
$$F = \frac{45000}{20} = 2250\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law:
- Net forward force over mass:
$$a = \frac{2250 - 750}{1200} = \frac{1500}{1200} = 1.25\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The car accelerates at $1.25\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Lorry on level road transitioning to incline with increased power

hints: At $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the driving force is $F = \frac{90000}{10} = 9000\text{ N}$.
Total opposing force up the slope is $R + mg\sin\theta = 3000 + 9000(10)(0.05) = 3000 + 4500 = 7500\text{ N}$.
Calculate acceleration: $a = \frac{9000 - 7500}{9000} = \frac{1500}{9000} = \frac{1}{6} \approx 0.167\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
For maximum steady speed, acceleration is zero, so $F = 7500\text{ N} \implies v_{\max} = \frac{90000}{7500} = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate driving force at $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and total opposing forces:
$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{90000}{10} = 9000\text{ N}$$
$$F_{\text{oppose}} = R + mg\sin\theta = 3000 + (9000)(10)(0.05) = 3000 + 4500 = 7500\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law along the incline:
$$F - F_{\text{oppose}} = ma \implies 9000 - 7500 = 9000a$$
$$1500 = 9000a \implies a = \frac{1500}{9000} = \frac{1}{6}\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.167\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Find maximum steady speed up the hill when $a = 0$:
$$F = 7500\text{ N} \implies v_{\max} = \frac{P}{F} = \frac{90000}{7500} = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate forces at $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
- Driving force is $9000\text{ N}$
- Opposing load (drag + gravity) is $3000 + 4500 = 7500\text{ N}$:
$$F_{\text{net}} = 9000 - 7500 = 1500\text{ N}$$

Calculate instantaneous acceleration:
- Dividing net force by lorry mass:
$$a = \frac{1500}{9000} = \frac{1}{6} \approx 0.167\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Determine hill top speed:
- When driving force drops to match the $7500\text{ N}$ load:
$$v_{\max} = \frac{90000}{7500} = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The lorry reaches a maximum climbing speed of $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates driving force at $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F = \frac{90000}{10} = 9000\text{ N}$ and gravity component $9000(10)(0.05) = 4500\text{ N}$.
Obtains acceleration $a = \frac{9000 - 3000 - 4500}{9000} = \frac{1500}{9000} = \frac{1}{6} \approx 0.167\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Sets $a = 0$ up the hill: $F = 3000 + 4500 = 7500\text{ N}$ and solves $v_{\max} = \frac{90000}{7500}$.
Obtains maximum steady speed up hill $v_{\max} = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 4: Car towing a trailer with engine power and towbar tension

hints: Driving force at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is $F = \frac{36000}{20} = 1800\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the whole system: $1800 - 600 = 2000a \implies 1200 = 2000a \implies a = 0.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the driving force produced by the engine at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{36000}{20} = 1800\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the entire car-trailer system ($m_{\text{total}} = 2000\text{ kg}$):
$$F - R_{\text{total}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$1800 - 600 = 2000a \implies 1200 = 2000a \implies a = 0.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the trailer to find towbar tension $T$:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} = m_{\text{trailer}} a$$
$$T - 200 = (600)(0.6) = 360 \implies T = 560\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find new tractive force:
- With $36\text{ kW}$ at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F = \frac{36000}{20} = 1800\text{ N}$$

Accelerate the entire combination:
- Net thrust divided by $2000\text{ kg}$:
$$a = \frac{1800 - 600}{2000} = 0.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Calculate towbar tension:
- Towbar must pull trailer drag and supply acceleration:
$$T = 200 + 600(0.6) = 560\text{ N}$$
The towbar experiences $560\text{ N}$ of tension.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates new driving force $F = \frac{36000}{20} = 1800\text{ N}$ and sets $(F - 600) = (1400 + 600)a$.
Obtains acceleration $a = \frac{1800 - 600}{2000} = \frac{1200}{2000} = 0.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Applies equation of motion to trailer $T - 200 = 600(0.6)$ to obtain tension $T = 560\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Capstone Practice 1: Quadratic resistance model and cubic equilibrium velocity

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 1: Quadratic resistance model and cubic equilibrium velocity

hints: At top speed $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$, driving force equals resistance: $\frac{64000}{40} = k(40^2) \implies 1600 = 1600k \implies k = 1$.
At speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the driving force is $F = \frac{64000}{20} = 3200\text{ N}$.
At speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, resistance is $R = kv^2 = 1(20^2) = 400\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law: $F - R = ma \implies 3200 - 400 = 1500a \implies 2800 = 1500a \implies a = 1.87\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Show that the constant $k = 1$ using the maximum speed condition on the level road:
$$F = R \implies \frac{P}{v_{\max}} = k v_{\max}^2$$
$$\frac{64000}{40} = k(40^2) \implies 1600 = 1600k \implies k = 1$$

Calculate driving force and resistance at instantaneous speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{64000}{20} = 3200\text{ N}$$
$$R = kv^2 = (1)(20^2) = 400\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to solve for acceleration:
$$F - R = ma \implies 3200 - 400 = 1500a$$
$$2800 = 1500a \implies a = \frac{2800}{1500} = \frac{28}{15}\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 1.8667\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 1.87\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine drag coefficient:
- Equating driving thrust to quadratic drag at $40\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$1600 = 1600k \implies k = 1$$
The drag constant is confirmed as $k = 1$.

$$V^3 + 750V = 90000 \implies V^3 + 750V - 90000 = 0$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Tractor pulling trailer on incline with power and tension analysis

hints: Total mass is $3200 + 1800 = 5000\text{ kg}$, and total resistance is $700 + 500 = 1200\text{ N}$.
Total gravity component down slope is $5000(10)(0.06) = 3000\text{ N}$, so driving force at steady speed is $1200 + 3000 = 4200\text{ N}$.
Maximum power is $P = 4200 \times 15 = 63000\text{ W} = 63\text{ kW}$.
For the trailer at steady speed: $T = R_{\text{trailer}} + m_{\text{trailer}}g\sin\alpha = 500 + 1800(10)(0.06) = 1580\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate total opposing forces acting on the combined tractor-trailer system ($m = 5000\text{ kg}$):
$$R_{\text{total}} = 700 + 500 = 1200\text{ N}$$
$$W_{\parallel,\text{total}} = m_{\text{total}} g \sin\alpha = (5000)(10)(0.06) = 3000\text{ N}$$
$$F = R_{\text{total}} + W_{\parallel,\text{total}} = 1200 + 3000 = 4200\text{ N}$$

Calculate maximum engine power in kilowatts:
$$P_{\max} = F v_{\max} = (4200)(15) = 63000\text{ W} = 63\text{ kW}$$

Consider the equilibrium of the trailer alone up the slope ($a = 0$):
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} - m_{\text{trailer}}g\sin\alpha = 0$$
$$T = 500 + (1800)(10)(0.06) = 500 + 1080 = 1580\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Sum all resistance and gravity forces:
- Friction and drag: $1200\text{ N}$
- Slope gravity component: $3000\text{ N}$:
$$F = 1200 + 3000 = 4200\text{ N}$$

Calculate engine power at top speed:
- Multiplying by $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P_{\max} = 4200 \times 15 = 63000\text{ W} = 63\text{ kW}$$

Find steady towbar tension:
- The towbar holds the trailer against its own drag and gravity:
$$T = 500 + 1080 = 1580\text{ N}$$
The towbar carries $1580\text{ N}$.

hints: Driving force at $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is $F = \frac{63000}{10} = 6300\text{ N}$.
Net forward force on the combined system is $6300 - 4200 = 2100\text{ N}$.
Divide by total mass ($5000\text{ kg}$) to get acceleration: $a = \frac{2100}{5000} = 0.42\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the trailer alone: $T - 1580 = 1800(0.42) \implies T = 1580 + 756 = 2336\text{ N} \approx 2340\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the driving force at instantaneous speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{63000}{10} = 6300\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the entire system ($m = 5000\text{ kg}$):
$$F - (R_{\text{total}} + W_{\parallel,\text{total}}) = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$6300 - 4200 = 5000a \implies 2100 = 5000a \implies a = 0.42\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the trailer alone along the slope:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} - m_{\text{trailer}}g\sin\alpha = m_{\text{trailer}} a$$
$$T - (500 + 1080) = (1800)(0.42)$$
$$T - 1580 = 756 \implies T = 2336\text{ N} \approx 2340\text{ N}$$

- Lower speed gives higher driving force:

Accelerate the rig:

$$a = \frac{6300 - 4200}{5000} = 0.42\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Determine increased towbar tension:
- Towbar must overcome trailer resistance, gravity, plus provide acceleration:
$$T = 1580 + 1800(0.42) = 2336\text{ N} \approx 2340\text{ N}$$
The towbar tension rises to $2340\text{ N}$ during acceleration.
